transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Um, yes… thank you. I’m not sure if this is, you know, a “real” reason to come in, but it’s been bothering me more than I expected.

Ever since we put in this brighter mirror in the bathroom, I keep noticing the skin around my cheeks and jaw. It looks uneven to me, or kind of saggy, I guess. My husband says he really can’t see what I’m talking about, so maybe I’m overreacting, but I can’t seem to stop noticing it.
How much has this concern about your skin been affecting your daily life or causing you distress?

It’s not… I mean, I’m still functioning. I still get my work done and everything, so I don’t want to make it sound dramatic.

But it has been affecting my mornings a bit. I spend extra time trying to look okay, and then I’ve had to rush into the courthouse a few times, which is embarrassing. And I’ve missed the start of yoga more than once because I couldn’t get out of the bathroom mirror fast enough, I guess.

Socially, it’s more like small things. I’ve skipped being in a few casual photos at book club or community events because I didn’t want to have to worry about how my face would look. So… it’s not ruining my life, but it’s definitely taking up more space than I’d like.
Have you noticed yourself becoming overly concerned about other parts of your body, or is most of your worry focused on the skin around your cheeks and jaw?

Mostly it’s just that area, I think… the skin around my cheeks and jaw. Since we got that brighter bathroom mirror, it sort of jumps out at me more, like it looks uneven or a little saggy.

I don’t think I’m picking apart my whole body or anything like that. My husband says he really doesn’t see what I mean, so I know it may sound minor, but that’s the thing I keep getting stuck on.

Have you found yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking the mirror, touching your face, or adjusting your appearance in specific ways, to try to fix or feel better about how your cheeks and jawline look?

A little, yes… I mean, not constantly, but most mornings I do end up checking my face from a few different angles in the mirror. I’ll put on a bit more makeup than I probably need before I leave for the courthouse, just to feel like it looks okay.

And sometimes I notice myself comparing my face to other women I see at work, which I know isn’t very helpful. I’ve also avoided being in casual pictures if I’m not feeling good about how my face looks. It sounds a bit silly saying it out loud, but yes, I guess I do those things.
Do you feel especially anxious or upset if you can’t check your face in the mirror or if you have to leave your house without putting on makeup to cover that area?

I wouldn’t say I get extremely upset… not like a panic or anything. But I do feel uncomfortable if I have to leave before I’ve had a chance to check it properly.

Most mornings I end up looking at my face from a few angles, and I’ll put on a little extra makeup before I go to the courthouse, just so I don’t feel as self-conscious. If I can’t do that, I guess I feel kind of unsettled, like I’m worried people will notice. It sounds a little vain, I know, but it’s more about feeling okay enough to get out the door.

Do you believe that the changes you’re noticing in your cheeks and jawline are something that other people would be able to see and judge, or do you feel like it’s something only you can really notice?

I guess… I worry that other people could see it, yes, even if I know that might not be completely realistic. To me, especially in that brighter bathroom mirror, the skin around my cheeks and jaw just looks uneven, or sort of saggy.

My husband says he really can’t see what I’m talking about, so maybe it’s more noticeable to me than to anyone else. But I still get stuck thinking, what if people do notice and are just being polite?
Do you find yourself avoiding social situations or feeling especially anxious in public because you think people might notice the skin on your cheeks or jaw?

Not really avoiding everything, no… I still go to work and I do what I need to do. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

But I guess it does affect little things. Some mornings I spend too long getting ready and then I’m rushing into the courthouse, which is embarrassing. And I’ve missed the beginning of yoga more than once because I was still trying to feel okay about how I looked.

Socially, it’s mostly photos. I’ve skipped being in a few casual pictures at book club or community events because I didn’t want to spend the whole time worrying about how my face would look. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you ever felt so preoccupied with the way your face looks that it’s hard to focus on anything else, or that it significantly interferes with your ability to enjoy normal activities?

I mean… I can usually still focus once I’m at work, and I do get my work done. I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t function.

But it does get in the way a little. The extra time I spend trying to look okay has made me rush into the courthouse a few mornings, and I’ve missed the start of yoga more than once because I was still fussing with my face or makeup.

And, like I mentioned, I’ve skipped being in a few casual photos at book club or community events, mostly because I didn’t want to spend the rest of the time worrying about how my face would look. So… not major, maybe, but it does take up more space than I’d like.
Would you say that your concern about your cheeks and jawline is more about feeling anxious in general, or is it specifically about how your face looks?

It feels pretty specific to how my face looks, I think. I mean, I do get anxious about it, but it starts with looking in that brighter bathroom mirror and noticing my cheeks and jawline.

To me the skin there looks uneven, or kind of saggy, even though my husband says he really doesn’t see what I’m talking about. So… I guess it’s not just general anxiety. It’s mostly tied to that part of my face.

Would you say that your concern about the skin on your cheeks and jaw is something that constantly runs through your mind, even when you're trying to focus on other things, or is it more of a background worry that only comes up in certain situations like looking in the mirror?

I wouldn’t say it’s constantly running through my mind, no. It’s more… it comes up in certain situations, especially when I’m in that brighter bathroom mirror.

That’s really when I start noticing the skin around my cheeks and jaw, and it looks uneven or kind of saggy to me. My husband says he can’t really see what I’m talking about, so maybe I’m making too much of it, but once I notice it, it’s hard not to keep checking. Is that what you mean?

Have you ever felt so upset or distressed about the way your cheeks and jaw look that it affected your ability to enjoy your day or caused you to withdraw from activities you used to participate in more fully?

A little, yes… I don’t want to overstate it, because I’m still getting my work done and everything. But it has affected my day sometimes.

Like, the extra time I spend trying to get ready and make my face look okay has made me rush into the courthouse a few mornings, which is embarrassing. And I’ve missed the start of yoga more than once because I was still fixing my makeup or checking my face.

I’ve also avoided being in a few casual photos at book club or community events, just because I didn’t want to spend the rest of the time worrying about how my cheeks or jaw would look in the picture. So… I guess I haven’t stopped doing everything, but I’m not participating as fully as I used to, if that makes sense.

When you’re concerned about how your cheeks and jaw look, do you feel like you have to perform certain behaviors or rituals—like checking your face repeatedly, adjusting your makeup a specific way, or mentally reviewing how you think you look—to feel reassured or to stop feeling anxious?

I guess… yes, somewhat. I don’t know if I’d call it a ritual exactly, because that sounds a little stronger than I mean, but most mornings I do check my face from a few different angles before I leave.

And if the cheeks or jaw look off to me, I’ll usually put on a little extra makeup and try to make it look better before I go to the courthouse. Sometimes at work I catch myself comparing my face to other women’s faces, which I know probably isn’t helpful.

And if I’m not feeling okay about how I look that day, I might avoid being in casual pictures. It’s not all day every day, but it does feel like I do those things to feel a bit more reassured. Does that make sense?

Do you find that the time you spend checking your face, adjusting your makeup, or thinking about how your cheeks and jaw look causes you a lot of distress or gets in the way of your day more than you’d like?

Yes… I think it does, more than I’d like to admit. I mean, I still get my work done, so it’s not like everything falls apart. But the extra time I spend checking and fixing my makeup has made me rush into the courthouse a few mornings, and that feels awful.

And I’ve missed the start of yoga more than once because I was still trying to get my face to look okay. I’ve also skipped being in a few casual photos at book club or community events because I didn’t want to spend the rest of the time worrying about how my cheeks or jaw would look.

So… yes, it gets in the way some. Maybe not severely, but enough that I don’t like it. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?

Would you say that your concern about your cheeks and jaw is more about feeling like you have a defect that makes you look abnormal, or is it more about feeling anxious in general and this just happens to be one of the things you worry about?

I think it’s more the first one… though I feel a little silly saying it that way. It’s not just general anxiety landing on my face, exactly.

I’m here because ever since we put in that brighter bathroom mirror, I keep noticing the skin around my cheeks and jaw. To me it looks uneven, or kind of saggy, like there’s something wrong with it. My husband says he really can’t see what I’m talking about, so I know it may not be as noticeable as it feels to me.

But when I see it, it does feel like a flaw in how I look, not just a random worry. Does that answer what you mean?

Yes… I think it does, more than I’d like to admit. I mean, I still get my work done, so it’s not like everything falls apart. But the extra time I spend checking and fixing my makeup has made me rush into the courthouse a few mornings, and that feels awful.

And I’ve missed the start of yoga more than once because I was still trying to get my face to look okay. I’ve also skipped being in a few casual photos at book club or community events because I didn’t want to spend the rest of the time worrying about how my cheeks or jaw would look.

So… yes, it gets in the way some. Maybe not severely, but enough that I don’t like it. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's concern about her facial appearance is better explained by a preoccupation with perceived physical defects (as in Body Dysmorphic Disorder - F45.22) or if it is more consistent with a manifestation of Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1), where appearance concerns are not the central focus but may be a source of secondary anxiety.
doctor.question: Would you say that your concern about your cheeks and jaw is more about feeling like you have a defect that makes you look abnormal, or is it more about feeling anxious in general and this just happens to be one of the things you worry about?

target_item.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because ever since we put in that brighter bathroom mirror, I keep noticing that the skin around my cheeks and jaw looks uneven or kind of saggy to me, even though my husband says he can’t really see what I’m talking about.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the concern is specifically about a perceived appearance defect in the cheeks and jaw rather than general anxiety, which directly matches preoccupation with perceived flaws in appearance.

patient.answer:
I think it’s more the first one… though I feel a little silly saying it that way. It’s not just general anxiety landing on my face, exactly.

I’m here because ever since we put in that brighter bathroom mirror, I keep noticing the skin around my cheeks and jaw. To me it looks uneven, or kind of saggy, like there’s something wrong with it. My husband says he really can’t see what I’m talking about, so I know it may not be as noticeable as it feels to me.

But when I see it, it does feel like a flaw in how I look, not just a random worry. Does that answer what you mean?

inference.note: The patient's concern is specifically about a perceived defect in their appearance (cheeks and jaw), with associated checking behaviors, reassurance-seeking, and avoidance related to this specific concern rather than general anxiety. This supports F45.22 (Body Dysmorphic Disorder) over F41.1 (Generalized Anxiety Disorder), which was ruled out as the focus of distress is clearly tied to physical appearance.
